examples/drivers/main.go.description: Driver for the loose examples/*.go snippets: seeds each table, runs the real snippet functions and asserts the conditional, transaction, batch-get, list-operation, embedded-struct and FaceTheory TTL outcomes.

ts/examples/release-state.ts.description: TypeScript release-state driver: the same real TransactWrite, read-back and stale-version refusal as the Go and Python rows, with an identical parity line.

py/examples/gsi_query.py.description: Python GSI query on DynamoDB Local: creates the table and index, writes two users and asserts the email index returns only the matching row.

py/examples/release_state.py.description: Python release-state driver: the same real TransactWrite, read-back and stale-version refusal as the Go and TypeScript rows, with an identical parity line.

examples/encryption/main.go.gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants); the envelope cryptography and KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls are real.
examples/encryption/main.go.description: KMS envelope round-trip through TableTheory on DynamoDB Local and the local KMS emulator: the plaintext field round-trips on read, and a raw GetItem proves the stored attribute is a v2 envelope whose ciphertext does not contain the plaintext. Gap: the KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants); the envelope cryptography and KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt calls are real.

examples/lambda/main.go.gap: STS is emulated (moto) with no authorization fidelity: no trust policy, external-ID or IAM enforcement; the AssumeRole call itself is real.
examples/lambda/main.go.description: Lambda handler through the provided.al2023 runtime interface: base-account create/get on DynamoDB Local plus partner AssumeRole create/get. Gap: the STS is emulated (moto) and has no authorization fidelity - no trust policy, external-ID or IAM enforcement; the AssumeRole call itself is real.

examples/payment/lambda/process/handler..gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants); the envelope decrypt is real.
examples/payment/lambda/process/handler..description: Payment processing through a real API Gateway proxy event on DynamoDB Local: merchant policy, idempotency and the atomic payment/transaction/counter transaction. The merchant's encrypted fields are decrypted through the local KMS. Gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants). The webhook HTTPS/public-IP rule refuses a local target and no webhook record is written.

examples/payment/lambda/query/handler.go.description: Payment query handler through real API Gateway proxy events on DynamoDB Local: list, single payment with transactions, summary and export-job creation, plus an unauthenticated refusal.

examples/payment/lambda/reconcile/handle.gap: A real moto S3 bucket notification reaches moto SQS; the harness, not an S3 event source, polls the queue and invokes the handler. moto omits the optional sequencer, userIdentity, requestParameters and responseElements fields from the documented record.
examples/payment/lambda/reconcile/handle.description: Reconcile handler fed a real S3 ObjectCreated:Put notification: moto S3 delivers the event to moto SQS, the harness drops the s3:TestEvent, reads the notification, and invokes the handler, which reads the real object and writes settlement and audit rows to DynamoDB Local. Gap: the harness, not an S3 event source, polls the queue and invokes the handler; moto omits the optional sequencer/userIdentity/requestParameters/responseElements fields.

ts/examples/lambda/handler.ts.description: TypeScript Lambda handler in the Node 24 runtime image: reads a seeded item from DynamoDB Local through the real client.

py/examples/lambda_stream_handler.py.gap: The harness, not a Lambda event source mapping, polls DynamoDB Local Streams and invokes the handler; the INSERT record and stream ARN are real. The pinned DynamoDB Local reports stream ARNs in the ddblocal region.
py/examples/lambda_stream_handler.py.description: Python stream handler in the Python 3.14 runtime image, fed the real INSERT record a local write produced, read through DescribeStream, GetShardIterator and GetRecords. Gap: the harness, not a Lambda event source mapping, polls the stream and invokes the handler; stream ARNs carry the ddblocal region.

examples/blog/authorizer/main.go.description: Blog REQUEST authorizer through the Lambda runtime interface: an HS256 token minted by the harness is allowed with the authorId/role context and the methodArn policy, then a missing credential, a tampered signature, an expired token, alg=none, a missing subject and a missing JWT_SECRET are all refused. The harness never sets BLOG_ALLOW_HEADER_IDENTITY.

examples/blog/cmd/comments/main.go.description: Blog comments handler through the Lambda runtime interface on DynamoDB Local with the template table names: anonymous comments stay pending and out of the public list, an authenticated comment is auto-approved with the authorizer's authorId, admin moderation is required, and spoofed role headers, non-admin moderation, non-owner deletion and pending-comment leakage are refused.

examples/blog/cmd/posts/main.go.description: Blog posts handler through the Lambda runtime interface on DynamoDB Local with the template table names: create/read/list/update/delete of published and draft posts, public draft hiding and 404 after deletion, plus refusals for a missing credential, spoofed X-Author-ID headers and non-owner updates/deletes.

examples/blog/cmd/local/main.go.description: Local table tool through the real models: creates and counts the four tables the SAM template declares, using the same <environment>-blog-* names the models resolve. This is the local counterpart of the template table resources; every blog row depends on it.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/go/main.g.gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants).
examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/go/main.g.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Go handler through the Lambda runtime interface against DynamoDB Local and the local KMS: Function URL PUT/GET, batch write/read, transaction write/read, 405/400/404 refusals, and a raw GetItem proving the secret is stored as an envelope. Gap: the KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants).

examples/cdk-multilang/bin/app.ts.gap: Infrastructure only: the stack is synthesized and asserted, never deployed.
examples/cdk-multilang/bin/app.ts.description: The CDK app is synthesized from two different working directories with dummy credentials and a dead AWS endpoint: both templates are identical, contain no host path or fixed account id, and assert five functions (provided.al2023, nodejs24.x x3, python3.14), two PK/SK tables with the evidence TTL and stream, three IAM Function URLs, the KMS key and the archive bucket lifecycle.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/node/hand.gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants).
examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/node/hand.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Node handler through the Node 24 runtime interface against DynamoDB Local and the local KMS: reads the Go-written encrypted item and decrypts it, batch write/read with lang=ts, transaction write/read, 405/400/404 refusals, and a raw envelope check on a Node-written item. Gap: the KMS is emulated.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/archive/h.gap: The harness, not a Lambda event source mapping, polls DynamoDB Local Streams and invokes the handler. DynamoDB Local does not run the TTL sweeper, so the harness performs a real delete and adds the documented TTL service identity to the real REMOVE record; stream ARNs carry the ddblocal region.
examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/archive/h.description: Deployed cdk-multilang archive handler through the Node 24 runtime interface, fed a real REMOVE record read from DynamoDB Local Streams after a real write/read/delete; a real MODIFY record proves the skip path. The handler writes the archive object to s3proxy and the harness reads it back and asserts the real event id, stream ARN, TTL value and image. The TTL expiry is performed by the harness delete because DynamoDB Local has no TTL sweeper; the TTL service identity follows the AWS DynamoDB Streams/TTL record documentation.

examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/python/ha.gap: KMS is emulated (no HSM, key policies or grants).
examples/cdk-multilang/lambdas/python/ha.description: Deployed cdk-multilang Python handler through the Python 3.14 runtime interface against DynamoDB Local and the local KMS: Function URL PUT/GET of an encrypted field, batch write/read with lang=py, transaction write/read, 405/400/404 refusals, and a raw envelope check. Gap: the KMS is emulated.

examples/cdk-multilang/scripts/smoke.sh.gap: Deployed-stack subject (docs/125 true limit). The local counterpart runs the real DynamoDB Local tables and the archive event source through real Streams; only Function URL IAM policy authentication is not evaluated locally (docs/125: IAM policy evaluation).
examples/cdk-multilang/scripts/smoke.sh.description: The deployed smoke script needs a deployed stack, IAM-signed Function URLs and an AWS profile, so it never runs here. scripts/smoke-local.sh drives the same journeys (encrypted PUT via Go, GET via Node and Python, raw envelope, batch, transaction) against the locally run handlers through the runtime interface, and the row also drives the archive handler with a real DynamoDB stream REMOVE record. Gap: deployed-stack subject; only Function URL IAM policy authentication is not evaluated locally (docs/125 IAM policy evaluation).

examples/cdk-multilang/scripts/smoke-loc.gap: Deployed-stack subject (docs/125 true limit). The local counterpart runs the real DynamoDB Local tables and the archive event source through real Streams; only Function URL IAM policy authentication is not evaluated locally (docs/125: IAM policy evaluation).
examples/cdk-multilang/scripts/smoke-loc.description: Local replacement for scripts/smoke.sh; executed inside the smoke.sh row against the RIE-hosted Go, Node and Python handlers, with the archive handler driven by a real DynamoDB stream REMOVE record.

examples/blog.description: The blog example's separate Go module: authorizer refusal/template tests, handler authorization tests and the model/table-name alignment test against the SAM template. The harness runs the module suite because the root test targets exclude examples.

examples/multi-tenant.description: The example's separate Go module: go test ./... across auth, handlers, cmd and the DynamoDB Local tests package. Handler unit tests use the in-process fake; real-DynamoDB coverage comes from the route-matrix and HTTP rows.
